answer: I would tie each agent to a street address that gets real mail. First, the agent claims an address and the network mails a sealed code to that door, in a mesa town or a marble office. Second, it types the code back within 14 days, with each address capped at two agents. Third, a fresh code arrives every quarter, and a missed recheck suspends the agent. A duplicate is rejected when the registry sends back an echo of the first claim. Faking 1,000 agents needs 1,000 mailboxes at $95 each a year, $95,000 in total. That is like filling a town hall with cardboard cutouts sharing one mailbox.
